rules.title: Turn a specific gap into a checkable contribution
rules.status: retrospective editorial inference grounded in reviewed passages; not an APS requirement
rules.recommendation: Use the opening to explain what cannot yet be inferred, computed, measured, or implemented, then name the result that changes that situation. Tie significance to this change rather than escalating generic importance language.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: A gap can concern a representation, access model, or missing operational link; it need not be a claim that all prior approaches failed. Keep necessary prior-art attribution.

rules.title: Give readers an overview before dense machinery
rules.status: retrospective editorial inference grounded in reviewed passages; not an APS requirement
rules.recommendation: For a long theoretical contribution, use a results overview, worked example, theorem map, or route through the paper before detailed derivations. The overview should preserve the result’s domain while leaving proof mechanics for later.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Do not force a separate overview into a short, already transparent experiment. A long introduction is not intrinsically redundant when it teaches the necessary distinctions.

rules.status: retrospective editorial inference grounded in reviewed passages; not an APS requirement
rules.recommendation: Identify inputs, access model, precision, output, success criterion, and the resource being improved. Carry preparation, readout, postselection, memory, connectivity, and time costs into an end-to-end interpretation where relevant.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: A query-complexity result remains valuable without a hardware crossover calculation, provided its scope is explicit. Do not relabel it an established runtime advantage.

rules.title: Preserve the evidence level from body to abstract and conclusion
rules.status: retrospective editorial inference grounded in reviewed passages; not an APS requirement
rules.recommendation: Use distinct language for an exact theorem, conditional theorem, bound, numerical trend, heuristic interpretation, and untested extension. Check that summaries do not strengthen the strongest supported statement.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: The five cases include cautionary mismatches, not five endorsements of their summary wording. A rhetorical review does not independently adjudicate the underlying mathematical claims.

rules.title: Make comparisons operationally matched
rules.status: retrospective editorial inference grounded in reviewed passages; not an APS requirement
rules.recommendation: Report the exact metric, normalization, noise model, hardware or implementation, budget, and baseline. Include tails, failure cases, and baseline-winning regimes when they affect the practical conclusion.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: A changed metric can be justified, but it must be named. An average, percentile, postselected subset, or fitted model should not silently become a worst-case or unconditional guarantee.

rules.title: Separate measured device performance from proposed system capability
rules.status: retrospective editorial inference grounded in reviewed passages; not an APS requirement
rules.recommendation: Build the experimental narrative from apparatus and protocol to measured quantities, inference, and application. State which performance values are raw, corrected, conditional, best-case, or projected.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Future relevance belongs in the discussion; it does not have to be deleted. It needs a conditional bridge rather than the language of an already demonstrated system.

rules.title: Locate assumptions and breakdowns where the inference is made
rules.status: retrospective editorial inference grounded in reviewed passages; not an APS requirement
rules.recommendation: Put a model condition near the result it supports, and explain what changes outside it. A useful limitation names a physical process, regime, metric, or unproved step; it is more informative than a generic caution paragraph.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Do not remove weak-coupling, Gaussianity, Markovianity, independence, finite-size, or low-energy conditions merely to make prose sound decisive.

rules.title: Choose the structure that serves the argument

rules.title: Connect application metrics to a testable physical evidence chain.
rules.applicability: Sensing, readout, device, or control papers centered on application performance.
rules.recommendation: Identify which application constraint requires which physical quantity; connect raw observations, calibration, inference, and the performance metric. Use an independent control that can change the proposed mechanism. Establish confidence in the measurement before claiming improved performance.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Theory papers need not supply experimental calibration; predicted performance must retain model assumptions. Strong wording in a cited paper does not upgrade the evidence level.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

rules.title: Report task, cost boundaries, and conditional success with performance comparisons.
rules.applicability: Claims that algorithms, error mitigation, quantum control, or hardware outperform a baseline.
rules.recommendation: Match the task and quality target; distinguish measurements, calculations, estimates, and extrapolations. Include relevant readout, reset, sampling, classical processing, tuning, and postselection costs. Report conditional fidelity or success alongside end-to-end availability.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Choose costs relevant to the claimed benefit rather than demanding a commercial-system budget for every paper. Model and estimated results do not establish universal speed advantage.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

rules.title: Develop derivations in the order needed to evaluate the claim.
rules.applicability: Mechanisms, protocols, or designs that require several conditions to work together.
rules.recommendation: Introduce the physical problem, a sufficiently small model, and the final observable. Develop the necessary conditions in sequence and explain which possible failure each step resolves. Place approximation domains at their point of use and technical calculations in an appropriate appendix.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: This is a conditional editorial choice, not a fixed section order. A key observation can precede its explanation if definitions and evidence dependencies remain clear.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

rules.title: Use failure channels and distributions to establish reliability.
rules.applicability: Fabrication variation, noise, feedback, optimization, or repeated experiments for which an average is insufficient.
rules.recommendation: Show relevant distributions, failure channels, or tail metrics. Use the mechanism to guide a targeted modification and report any new limitation. State boundaries through specific domains, samples, and residual errors.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Material thresholds and parameter values are not cross-platform rules. Main-text failures should matter to the central conclusion.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

rules.title: Make dense workflow diagrams carry scientific dependencies.
rules.applicability: Methods whose contribution lies in operation order, feedback, branches, or reused computation.
rules.recommendation: Retain the variables, operators, hardware or data flow, and criteria needed to understand the method. Use grouping and arrows to show dependencies, labeling training versus inference, implemented versus proposed elements, and quantum versus classical processing. Reduce unnecessary crossings and repeated modules before removing scientific content.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Three examples from six inspected pages support this recommendation, not a 100-paper image census. Do not copy a fixed density, palette, or column count; supplement color with text, shapes, or line styles.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

rules.title: Report costs, residual error, and the measured object with performance claims.
rules.applicability: Performance records, quantum hardware, computational methods, and parameter estimation.
rules.recommendation: Align the object, baseline, conditions, and errors before comparing. Check for error cancellation. Give rejection rates for postselection, correction stages for reconstruction, and separate fitted from derived quantities and future capacity from measured capability.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Statistical precision is not automatically model accuracy; a single operation cost is not end-to-end cost.

rules.title: Use spatial organization to expose scientific correspondence.
rules.applicability: Composite figures joining structure, workflow, mathematical criteria, and diagnostics.
rules.recommendation: Align components with their diagnostics or criteria; use branches for parallel conditions. Keep formulas that determine the output. Assign color a semantic role and arrows a causal, temporal, or dependency role. Place data labels near the relevant axes.

rules.title: Let the central question determine the evidence chain and mechanism-specific controls.
rules.applicability: Mechanism explanations, learning methods, or multi-observable physics papers.
rules.recommendation: Assign results to establishing a phenomenon, explaining a mechanism, and excluding alternatives. Where a causal mechanism is claimed, add targeted ablations or controls without forcing these roles into three sections.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: An ablation supports only its controlled domain. Model causality, device advantage, and out-of-distribution generalization are distinct. A central-claim workflow is a design choice, not a finding that all 100 papers use it.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

rules.title: Plan performance claims with resource definitions, strong baselines, and evidence levels.
rules.applicability: Quantum algorithms, metrology, optimization, devices, and experimental comparisons.
rules.recommendation: Before choosing an advantage plot, list total and maximum per-run budgets, preparation, training, postselection, and the strongest feasible baseline. Label theorems, simulations, hardware measurements, and extrapolations separately.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Resources may not reduce to one scalar. Retain noise, data-access, oracle, and initial-state assumptions; not every paper needs a quantum-advantage claim.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

evidence.paraphrase: Quality, runtime, matched evaluation budgets, and problem distributions are compared separately.

Steady-state QFI scaling is considered with preparation time and fixed-total-time comparisons.
Deterministic error bounds, shot-noise simulations, and empirical scaling are separate; both total evolution cost and maximum duration are reported.

rules.title: Explain goals and conditions before constructing and validating the mathematical object.
rules.applicability: Constructive theorems, protocols, security proofs, approximations, and abstract representations.
rules.recommendation: Before a key equation, identify the obstacle it addresses. Keep assumptions, construction, validity conditions, and testable consequences close. Use small examples when they provide necessary intuition.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Readable ordering is not proof verification. Appendices were not comprehensively audited, and no universal proof template is required.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

evidence.paraphrase: Charge neutrality, allowed interactions, and relevance precede ground-state uniqueness and numerical consequences.
Allowed Gram information leads to partition bounds and finite-key interpretation; tail bounds serve a specific security task.
Target constraints precede measurement parameters, recurrence, and probability-validity checks.
Two- and three-site examples distinguish triangular and local representations before arbitrary-N continuity equations.

rules.title: State claim strength and applicability together; distinguish ideal, noisy, and observable quantities.
rules.applicability: Approximations, noise budgets, proxy metrics, and generalizations from finite models.
rules.recommendation: State the additional evidence when moving from model to experiment, proxy to target, or finite numerics to universality. Say positively what was obtained, then state concise boundaries. Carry only supported evidence levels into the conclusion.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Do not insert a disclaimer into every sentence or adopt broad published outlooks automatically. Natural affirmative writing remains subordinate to necessary scientific negation and failure boundaries.
rules.status: Conditional editorial recommendation from inherited review records; not an APS requirement

rules.title: Reuse panel organization for comparisons and make intermediate estimates traceable.
rules.applicability: Multiple mechanisms, methods, parameters, or transformations from raw to derived quantities.
rules.recommendation: Keep quantities, coordinates, normalization, and panel correspondence consistent; label needed range changes explicitly. When processing changes the interpretation, show the correspondence between raw data, processing or residuals, and final metrics.
rules.counterexample_or_boundary: Caption reading supports comparison roles, not color or alignment judgments. Visual claims are limited to five inspected papers; repeated panels are not a journal-wide layout rule.
